question: Will Russia enter Vasylivka by July 31, 2026?
rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Vasylivka, Donetsk Oblast, (48.357760° N, 37.038017° E) between market creation and the specified date (ET).

Territory will be considered captured if any part of the specified territory is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. 

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War / AEI Critical Threats Project
evidence.excerpt: Russian forces continued offensive operations in the Pokrovsk direction on July 8 and 9 but did not advance.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War / AEI Critical Threats Project
evidence.excerpt: Geolocated footage published on July 5 and 8 shows Ukrainian forces striking Russian forces in central and southeastern Rodynske (north of Pokrovsk) respectively, indicating that Russian forces maintain positions or recently advanced in the area.

Aside from Kostiantynivka, Russia’s Defence Ministry said on Saturday it had taken five villages in eastern Ukraine: Shyikivka, Novyi Myr, Cherneshchyna and Druzhelyubivka in Kharkiv region, and Vasylivka in Donetsk region. Reuters could not verify the battlefield reports.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War / AEI Critical Threats Project
evidence.excerpt: ISW has only observed evidence to assess that Russian forces seized or infiltrated into 64 settlements and seized or infiltrated approximately 621.7 square kilometers across the theater since the start of 2026, and that Russian forces have seized or infiltrated into 20 settlements and gained or infiltrated approximately 30.42 square kilometers in the theater in June 2026.

evidence.publisher: Ukrinform, citing the Ukrainian General Staff
evidence.excerpt: According to Ukrinform, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine released the operational update as of 16:00 on Thursday, July 9. In the Pokrovsk sector, Russian troops made seven attempts to push Ukrainian forces from their positions near Dorozhne, Novooleksandrivka, and Udachne, advancing toward Shevchenko and Serhiivka. One engagement is ongoing.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War / AEI Critical Threats Project
evidence.excerpt: Geolocated footage published on June 4 indicates that Ukrainian forces recently advanced in western Rodynske (north of Pokrovsk). ISW assesses that Russian forces no longer maintain a continuous forward line of own troops (FLOT) in western and central Rodynske, given that footage observed since April 24 indicates that Ukrainian forces have maintained or regained positions in western or central Rodynske. A Russian milblogger claimed on June 5 that Russian forces advanced north of Vasylivka (northwest of Pokrovsk).
